kaps_punt: Oplossings: oplossings is ook mengsels; sommige oplossings kan gemaak word deur die vermenging van 'n vaste en 'n vloeistof soos suiker en water, sout en water; oplossings is eenvormig in voorkoms en die vastestowwe kan nie gesien word na vermenging nie. Onoplosbare stowwe: Sommige vastestowwe sal nie 'n oplossing in die water vorm nie (onoplosbare vastestowwe).

items.bewering: Jy weet al wat 'n mengsel is: twee of meer stowwe wat saam gemeng is.
items.bron: Chemistry LibreTexts 9.1 Solutions (chem.libretexts.org, USC Upstate CHEM U109): a solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances. Grade 6 simplification (omits 'not chemically combined') is not false.

items.bewering: Gooi nou 'n teelepel suiker in 'n glas water en roer goed. Na 'n rukkie sien jy geen suikerkorrels meer nie. Tog is die water en die suiker albei nog in die glas. Daarom is suikerwater ook 'n mengsel wat ons 'n oplossing noem.
items.bron: ACS Middle School Chemistry, Chapter 5 lessons 5.4 and 5.6 (acs.org/middleschoolchemistry): sugar molecules separate and spread through the water but stay whole sucrose molecules; LibreTexts 9.1: a solution is a homogeneous mixture.

items.bewering: Om 'n vaste stof in 'n vloeistof te meng is een manier om 'n oplossing te maak. Suiker en water is een paar, en sout en water is nog een.
items.bron: Scientific American, 'Salty Science: How to Separate Soluble Solutions' (scientificamerican.com): salt is soluble in water, sand is not; ACS Middle School Chemistry ch. 5 for sugar.

items.bewering: Strooi 'n teelepel sout in 'n glas water en roer. Die wit korrels word al hoe kleiner tot jy hulle nie meer sien nie. Ons sê dan die sout het opgelos.
items.bron: Scientific American, 'Salty Science' (scientificamerican.com): when salt dissolves you can no longer see it, but it is still in the water. A teaspoon (about 6 g) in a glass is far below salt's solubility (about 360 g per litre), so it dissolves completely.

items.bewering: Die water in 'n glas soutwater lyk bo dieselfde as onder en in die middel. Ons noem 'n oplossing eenvormig omdat dit oral in die houer dieselfde lyk. Jy sien ook geen korrels van die vaste stof meer nie.
items.bron: Lumen Learning General Chemistry, 'Colloids' (courses.lumenlearning.com/suny-binghamton-chemistry/chapter/colloids-2): a solution is transparent, its particles are invisible and do not settle; LibreTexts 9.1: homogeneous mixture.

items.bewering: 'n Oplossing is deursigtig, en dit beteken jy kan daardeur sien. Dit mag wel 'n kleur hê.
items.bron: Lumen Learning General Chemistry, 'Colloids': 'A solution may be colored, but it is transparent'.

items.bewering: Rooibostee sonder melk is rooibruin en tog kan jy daardeur sien.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Rooibos' and Carmien Tea (carmientea.co.za, South African producer): oxidised rooibos gives a reddish-brown infusion. Mapping checked: the example is used only for 'coloured but still see-through', which holds. Brewed tea is commonly used as an example of a coloured solution. Some sources call tea colloidal, but the lesson does not rest anything on that.

items.bewering: Roer 'n teelepel suiker in jou tee tot jy geen korrels meer sien nie. Die eerste sluk is net so soet soos die laaste. Die suiker is dus oral in die tee al sien jy dit nie.
items.bron: LibreTexts 9.1 and Lumen 'Colloids': a solution is homogeneous and its particles do not settle, so the composition, and therefore the sweetness, is the same throughout once the sugar has dissolved and been stirred. 'eerste'/'laaste' here mean first and last sip, not a historical superlative.

items.bewering: Party mense sê die suiker het in die tee gesmelt, maar dit is verkeerd. Smelt gebeur wanneer een stof warm word en self 'n vloeistof word. 'n Blokkie ys in die son smelt en word water.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Melting' (britannica.com/science/melting): melting is the change of a solid into a liquid when heat is applied; LibreTexts 13.11 Melting (Introductory Chemistry, CK-12): ice changing to water is melting.

items.bewering: Vir oplos het jy twee stowwe nodig wat saam gemeng word, soos suiker en water. Suiker los ook in koue water op sonder dat iets verhit word. Die suiker word nie self 'n vloeistof nie, maar versprei deur die water.
items.bron: ACS Middle School Chemistry, Lesson 5.6 'Does Temperature Affect Dissolving?' (acs.org): sugar dissolves in cold water as well, just more slowly; Lesson 5.4: water molecules separate the sugar molecules, which spread through the water.

items.bewering: Sommige vaste stowwe vorm nie 'n oplossing in water nie. Ons sê hulle is onoplosbaar, en sand is een voorbeeld.
items.bron: Scientific American, 'Salty Science' (scientificamerican.com): sand is insoluble in water and gradually sinks to the bottom.

items.bewering: Mieliemeel en meel los ook nie in water uit die kraan op nie. Dieselfde geld vir mielieblom en stampmielies in water uit die kraan.
items.bron: ScienceDirect overview 'Fractionation of wheat and wheat flour into starch and gluten' (Van der Borght et al., J. Cereal Sci.): flour is about 70-75% starch plus gluten protein, both insoluble in cold water; ScienceBob 'Oobleck' and the ResearchGate thread on cornstarch solubility in cold water: cornstarch grains are suspended, not dissolved, and settle out. Only a few percent of flour (albumins, sugars) is water-soluble, so 'los nie op nie' is a fair Grade 6 statement. The 'water uit die kraan' qualifier correctly excludes hot water, where starch swells. Samp is broken dried maize kernels (Wikipedia 'Samp'), made of the same starch.

items.bewering: Kerriepoeier en vlapoeier gee die water 'n kleur, maar die meeste van die poeier los nie op nie.
items.bron: Vlapoeier: Open Food Facts and Pick n Pay product listings for Moir's Custard Powder (South African brand): maize starch/flour, salt, flavouring and colourants (E104, E124). The dyes and salt dissolve, but the starch that makes up most of the powder does not. Kerriepoeier: Wikipedia 'Curry powder': a blend of ground spices, coloured mainly by turmeric; ScienceDirect (Food Chemistry, S0308814616311244) and ResearchGate: curcumin, turmeric's colouring, is poorly water-soluble. Ground plant material does not dissolve. 'die meeste' is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: Roer 'n lepel meel in 'n glas water. Die water word troebel en jy kan nie meer mooi daardeur sien nie. As die glas 'n rukkie staan, sak die meeste meel stadig na die bodem.
items.blok: Wat jy by 'n onoplosbare stof sien
items.bron: Plainpaper.blog 'Does flour dissolve better in warm or cold water' and ResearchGate 'Cornstarch solubility in cold water': flour and starch form a suspension in water and settle to the bottom over time. The cloudiness is what a suspension looks like (Lumen 'Colloids': suspensions are cloudy and settle).

items.bewering: By sand en stampmielies sien jy die stukkies gou op die bodem lê.
items.blok: Wat jy by 'n onoplosbare stof sien
items.bron: Sand: Scientific American 'Salty Science': sand gradually sinks to the bottom. Stampmielies: dry maize kernels have a true density of about 1 220-1 250 kg/m3 (Taylor & Francis, 'Physical characteristics of maize grain as influenced by varietal and moisture differences', 2022), which is denser than water, so the broken kernels in samp sink quickly.

items.bewering: Kerriepoeier en vlapoeier maak die water ook troebel, en die meeste poeier sak uit.
items.blok: Wat jy by 'n onoplosbare stof sien
items.bron: Vlapoeier part confirmed: it is mostly maize starch, which makes water cloudy and settles (ResearchGate cornstarch thread; ScienceBob Oobleck). Kerriepoeier part not settled: that most curry powder settles out is supported only by weak sources (a turmeric trade site, aquaconnectexim.com, and a parenting blog, snuggymom.com). A curry maker's page (kennedyscurry.com) returned no content. No university, museum or reference source was found for how a mixed spice powder behaves in cold water. Curry blends contain spices such as pepper and oily ground seeds, and part of that can float on the surface rather than sink. The only other results were school textbook pages (NCERT), which were not opened or used. For a person: the claim is probably broadly right after standing, but it is unverified. The diagnostic in the next block ('as jy dit nog sien of dit na die bodem sak') still classifies curry powder correctly either way, so cutting 'en die meeste poeier sak uit' for curry powder, or limiting it to vlapoeier, costs the lesson nothing.

items.bewering: 'n Oplossing bly deursigtig, en niks sak daarin uit nie.
items.blok: Wat jy by 'n onoplosbare stof sien
items.bron: Lumen Learning General Chemistry 'Colloids' and CK-12 Flexi: the particles of a solution are too small to settle and do not settle out on standing.

items.bewering: 'n Stof is oplosbaar as dit in water kan oplos, soos suiker en sout. 'n Stof is onoplosbaar as dit nie in water oplos nie.
items.blok: Hoe jy die twee uitmekaar ken
items.bron: Merriam-Webster and Collins, 'soluble': able to be dissolved in a liquid, especially or usually water. Tying the words to water matches everyday and CAPS usage and is not false.

items.bewering: Die ondersoek toets wat jy sien nadat jy 'n teelepel van elke stof in 'n glas water geroer het. Die stof is oplosbaar as die water deursigtig en oral dieselfde bly. Die stof is onoplosbaar as jy dit nog sien of dit na die bodem sak.
items.blok: Hoe jy die twee uitmekaar ken
items.bron: Lumen 'Colloids': solutions are transparent (may be coloured) and do not settle, while suspensions are cloudy and settle. Mapping checked against every substance in the lesson: sugar and salt (clear, uniform) come out soluble; sand, samp, flour, mielieblom, curry and custard powder (cloudy, visible or settling) come out insoluble. So the test sorts the lesson's own examples correctly. 'jy dit nog sien' must be read as the grains, not a colour, and the lesson says earlier that a solution may be coloured.

items.bewering: oplos: Wanneer die deeltjies van 'n stof losraak en tussen die deeltjies van 'n vloeistof meng, sodat jy geen korrels meer kan sien nie.
items.bron: ACS Middle School Chemistry, Lesson 5.4 'Why Does Water Dissolve Sugar?' (acs.org): water molecules pull the solute particles apart and they mix among the water molecules. Read on its own, the particle picture is accurate at this level.

items.bewering: oplossing: 'n Mengsel waarin een of meer stowwe in 'n vloeistof opgelos het. Dit lyk oral dieselfde.
items.bron: LibreTexts 9.1: a solution is a homogeneous mixture in which a solute is dissolved in a solvent. Limiting it to a liquid solvent leaves out solid and gas solutions, which is a Grade 6 simplification, not a falsehood.

items.bewering: oplosbaar: Iets wat in water kan oplos, soos suiker en sout.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster and Collins, 'soluble' (especially or usually in water); Scientific American 'Salty Science' for salt.

items.bewering: onoplosbaar: Iets wat nie in water oplos nie, soos sand.
items.bron: Scientific American 'Salty Science': sand is insoluble in water.

items.bewering: smelt: Wanneer 'n vaste stof warm word en in 'n vloeistof verander.
items.bron: Britannica 'Melting': the change of a solid into a liquid when heat is applied.

items.bewering: eenvormig: Oral dieselfde, sodat geen deel anders lyk as 'n ander deel nie.
items.bron: LibreTexts 9.1: a homogeneous mixture has the same composition and appearance throughout.

items.bewering: deursigtig: Wanneer jy deur iets kan sien, soos deur skoon glas.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'transparent': able to be seen through, so that objects beyond are clearly visible; clear glass is the standard example.

items.bewering: troebel: Wanneer 'n vloeistof vol klein stukkies is en nie meer helder is nie.
items.bron: Lumen 'Colloids': suspensions and colloids look cloudy because of suspended particles, unlike clear solutions. Droplets, as in milk, also count as 'klein stukkies' at this level.

opsomming: All but one claim checks out: no source I would defend confirms that most curry powder sinks after it is stirred into water (part of it may float). A person should decide whether to cut that phrase for curry powder or limit it to custard powder.
